title: The Silent Weaver: Uva's Loom of Fate
description:
Deep within the emerald hills of Sri Lanka's Uva province, a whisper travels on the evening breeze—a legend of an ancient loom. They say it works by itself after dark, weaving not cloth, but the very fabric of tomorrow's sorrows. This story explores what happens when a curious mind dares to glimpse its chilling work.

This episode is a retelling of Sri Lankan folklore, with characters and events dramatised for your listening pleasure. Prepare for a quiet chill.
fiction_note: Based on Sri Lankan folklore; characters and events are dramatised.

scenes.narration: Have you ever heard a sound… a rhythmic, tireless clatter… from an empty room, deep in the night? In the remote reaches of Sri Lanka’s Uva hills, where red earth roads wind through jak trees and the air smells of rain on hot ground, they speak of such a thing. Not a ghost, not an animal… but a loom. An ancient, wooden loom, said to sit in an abandoned mud house on the edge of the jungle. It moves by itself after dark, they say, weaving a tapestry of future tragedies. And anyone who glimpses it working… will see their own misfortune unfold.
visuals: Wide shot of a winding red-earth road through dense jak tree forest at dusk, the road wet from recent rain, 50mm lens, film grain.
Detail shot of a gnarled jak tree branch, dark green leaves, water droplets clinging, blurring into the forest background, soft evening light, shallow depth of field.

scenes.narration: Suman was a young man, a city boy really, visiting his mother’s ancestral village near Ella. He found the old stories charming, quaint, a nice break from the bustle of Colombo. The legend of the weaving loom was just another one. Until one evening, his grandfather, Seeya, a man whose eyes held the wisdom of generations, spoke of it with a tremor in his voice. “Putha,” Seeya said, stirring his cup of plain tea, “some things… it’s best not to look too close. Some futures are not meant for mortal eyes.”
visuals: Wide shot of a simple, open-air village house verandah at twilight, a kerosene lamp casting warm light, an elderly man (Seeya) sitting on a wooden bench, back to viewer, sipping tea, 35mm lens.
Detail shot of a steaming glass of plain tea on a rough wooden table, the flickering light of a kerosene lamp reflecting on the glass, blurred background of a village path.

scenes.narration: That night, Suman lay awake, the geckos clicking on the mud walls, the distant thrum of temple drums carrying on the breeze. He heard it then. Faint at first, a distant, rhythmic *thwack-thwack-clatter*. It was subtle, almost part of the night sounds, but distinct. His heart gave a little jump. He tried to dismiss it as the wind, or perhaps an old farmer working late. But Seeya’s words echoed. 'An empty house, Suman. Nobody lives there now. Hasn't for sixty years.' The sound persisted, a tireless, ghostly rhythm.
visuals: Interior wide shot of a sparsely furnished bedroom in a village house at night, moonlight filtering through a small window onto a sleeping mat, Suman's silhouette visible under a mosquito net, 50mm lens, long exposure.
Detail shot of a small, open window at night, heavy monsoon rain starting to fall outside, blurred distant lights, the sound of geckos unseen on the sill, ambient light.

scenes.narration: A strange mix of dread and a powerful curiosity began to brew in Suman. He was a modern man, after all. There had to be a logical explanation. A branch scraping, an old gate. Anything but a self-weaving loom of fate. The old house was just a short walk, maybe a kilometer, down a narrow, overgrown path off the main village track. He thought about Seeya’s warning, the way his knuckles whitened on his tea cup. But the rhythmic *clack-clack* was a challenge, a dare, floating on the cool night air. He had to see for himself.
visuals: Wide shot of a young man (Suman) in silhouette, standing at the threshold of a village house doorway, looking out into the moonlit night, overgrown jungle path visible, 85mm lens.
Detail shot of Suman's bare feet on a cool, rough cement floor, the path outside just visible, a faint glow of moonlight, suggesting a hesitant step forward.

scenes.narration: He slipped out of the house just after midnight, the kerosene lamp left burning low in the main room. The red-earth path felt cooler under his bare feet, damp with dew. Crickets chirped a frenzied symphony. He walked past sleeping huts, the smell of woodsmoke lingering. The jungle pressed close, its shadows deep and ancient. The old house loomed ahead, a darker shape against the pale moonlight, its mud walls crumbling, its tiled roof sagging. A faint, almost imperceptible *thrum-thrum* grew louder as he approached. His heart beat like a hummingbird’s wings.
visuals: Wide shot of a young man's back (Suman) walking along a narrow, overgrown red-earth path at night, illuminated by soft moonlight, dense jungle shadows on either side, 35mm lens.
Detail shot of the overgrown path, tall grass and ferns brushing against a bare leg, the faint light of the moon creating long shadows from the foliage.

scenes.narration: The air around the house was heavy, still, carrying the scent of damp earth and decay. The wooden gate hung crookedly on rusted hinges, groaning when he pushed it open. He stepped into the overgrown garden, past skeletal frangipani trees. The front door was ajar, a black rectangle. He pushed it slowly. It scraped on the floorboards, a sound like an old man clearing his throat. Inside, the silence was overwhelming, oppressive. Dust motes danced in the slivers of moonlight piercing the gaps in the roof tiles. Then, from deeper within, he heard it again. Clearer now. The loom.
visuals: Wide shot of an old, abandoned mud house at night, crumbling walls, sagging tiled roof, a wooden door slightly ajar, bathed in cold moonlight, overgrown garden in foreground, 28mm lens.
Detail shot of a rusted, ornate metal hinge on a weathered wooden door, a sliver of eerie moonlight shining through the gap into a dark interior, cobwebs visible.

scenes.narration: He moved towards the sound, his breath catching in his throat. Through an open doorway, he peered into a small, windowless room. The air was thick with the smell of old wood and something else… something faintly metallic, like dried blood. In the center, bathed in a pale, almost phosphorescent moonlight filtering through a high, broken tile, stood the loom. Its wooden frame was ancient, dark with age. And it was moving. Shuttles flew back and forth, pedals pumped, threads danced and twisted. No hand guided it. It worked by itself, tirelessly, purposefully, weaving a dark, intricate pattern.
visuals: Interior wide shot of a very dusty, dimly lit room in an old mud house, the large wooden loom in the center, working autonomously, illuminated by a pale shaft of moonlight from above, cobwebs hanging, 35mm lens.
Detail shot of the loom's wooden shuttles flying across the warp threads, seen in the eerie moonlight, no hands visible, threads themselves seem to glow faintly, extremely shallow depth of field.

scenes.narration: Suman felt a strange pull, a morbid fascination. He stepped closer, peering at the weaving. The threads were not cotton or silk, but seemed to be made of shadow and moonlight, shimmering with an unsettling energy. As he focused, the patterns on the loom began to shift, to coalesce, forming images. Horrific images. He saw a familiar road, the main road from Ella to Kandy, rain-slicked. He saw a red tuk-tuk, veering wildly. And then… he saw himself. He saw the flash of metal, the screech of tires, the sudden, terrible impact. His own face, contorted in fear, reflected in a broken mirror shard. It was his future. His end.
visuals: Abstract wide shot of shimmering, dark threads on an ancient loom, twisting and forming indistinct, unsettling patterns under pale moonlight, hinting at images without being explicit, 100mm macro lens.
Impressionistic detail shot of a broken mirror shard on the dusty floor, reflecting a distorted, fearful eye of an unseen observer, the loom's ghostly weave blurred in the background, very low light.

scenes.narration: A cold dread seized Suman, far worse than any fear he had known. His legs felt like jelly. He stumbled back, a choked gasp escaping his lips. He had seen it. His own woven fate. The loom, as if acknowledging his presence, slowed its frantic rhythm. The shuttles moved sluggishly, then stopped altogether. The threads hung limp, dull. The room plunged back into oppressive silence, broken only by Suman's ragged breathing. He scrambled backward, turning, fleeing the house, the smell of damp earth and decay replaced by the bitter taste of terror in his mouth.
visuals: Wide shot from behind Suman, his silhouette rapidly retreating from the loom room doorway, arms outstretched as if pushing through unseen obstacles, the loom now still and dark, lit only by faint moonlight, 28mm lens.
Detail shot of a bare foot, covered in red dust, stumbling over cracked floorboards, moving quickly away from a dark interior, lit by a single, distant shaft of moonlight.

scenes.narration: He ran all the way back to his grandfather’s house, not stopping, not looking back. The memory of the loom, the vision, burned behind his eyes. He couldn’t unsee it. He told no one. How could he? Who would believe such a thing? The next few weeks were a blur of nervous waiting. Every tuk-tuk on the road, every rain shower, every sudden noise sent a jolt of ice through his veins. He tried to avoid the main road, tried to avoid tuk-tuks. But the vision… it was so clear. He felt like a puppet, dancing on strings already woven.
visuals: Wide shot of Suman's back, sitting hunched and withdrawn on a verandah bench in daylight, looking out blankly, the vibrant village life continuing around him but he is detached, 50mm lens.
Detail shot of Suman's hands, clasped tightly, knuckles white, resting on his knees, a tremor barely visible, the rough texture of his sarong visible, natural light.

scenes.narration: Months passed. The dread became a constant companion. Then, one day, his mother fell ill. A sudden, terrible fever. Suman rushed to the hospital in Kandy. The quickest way, the only way, was a hired tuk-tuk on the main road. The sky was darkening, heavy with monsoon clouds. The first drops of rain splattered on the windshield. His vision flashed before his eyes. He knew. He gripped the seat, eyes wide, watching the road unfold. The loom had shown him, hadn't it? What would you do, knowing your fate was already spun? Sometimes, my friends, it’s not the unknown that truly frightens us, but the certainty of it. If you found this story unsettling, perhaps follow us… for more quiet chills from Ceylon Dread.
visuals: Wide shot from inside a moving tuk-tuk, looking out at a rain-slicked main road (Ella-Kandy highway), distant headlights blurring in the monsoon rain, the driver's silhouette at the front, 35mm lens, atmospheric.
Detail shot of a hand gripping the metal frame of a tuk-tuk seat, raindrops blurring on the window next to it, the road's reflection distorted on the wet surface, low light, high contrast.

Vertical shot of a small, open window in a mud wall at night, rain starting to fall outside, blurred distant village lights, a sense of quiet tension.

shorts.title: A Glimpse of Fate
shorts.narration: Driven by an unsettling curiosity, Suman crept into the abandoned mud house where the legendary loom was said to reside. The air was heavy with decay, the silence oppressive. Then, from a windowless room, he heard it again – clearer now. He peered in. In the pale, phosphorescent moonlight, an ancient wooden loom worked by itself. Shuttles flew, pedals pumped, threads danced, weaving a dark, intricate pattern. Suman felt a morbid pull. As he stepped closer, the patterns began to shift, coalescing into images. Horrific images. He saw a familiar, rain-slicked road. A red tuk-tuk. And then… he saw himself. His own face, twisted in fear, in a terrible impact. The loom was weaving his end. The full story is on our channel.
visuals: Vertical shot of a dark, narrow doorway into a dusty, abandoned room, a sliver of eerie moonlight just touching the threshold, foreboding atmosphere.
Vertical shot of the ancient wooden loom, center frame, working autonomously, illuminated by a pale shaft of moonlight from above, focus on the moving shuttles, no hands visible.
Vertical shot of shimmering, dark threads on the loom, twisting into indistinct, unsettling patterns under pale moonlight, suggesting forming images.
Vertical shot of a distorted, fearful eye reflected in a small, broken mirror shard on the dusty floor, the loom's ghostly weave blurred in the background.
Vertical shot of Suman's silhouette, seen from behind, rapidly retreating from the loom room doorway, hands covering his mouth in shock, the loom now still and dark.
